title: Hepatitis B PCR (viral load)
what: This blood test shows how much hepatitis B virus is in your blood right now.
why: If you have hepatitis B, to decide whether you need treatment and to follow it. Also in pregnancy for women with hepatitis B.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come in a few days
tell_doctor: If you take medicines for hepatitis B
If you are pregnant or planning a pregnancy
If you have hepatitis C, hepatitis D, or HIV
If you take medicines that weaken the immune system

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You usually do not need to fast strictly, but it is better to come 3 to 4 hours after a light, non-fatty meal. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: If you are on treatment, take your pills as scheduled. Do not stop or skip them on your own.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: A sleeve you can easily roll up above the elbow.

bring: Your referral or list of tests
Liver ultrasound reports, if you have them
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tied above your elbow, and you are asked to clench your fist a few times
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick. Blood fills the tubes in a few seconds
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse, and they will help you lie down
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
It helps to compare with past results. The doctor looks at how it changes
Your result is confidential. Only you or your doctor will get it.
red_flags: The puncture site is very swollen, painful, and red

faq.q: How often do I need this test?
faq.a: Usually once or a few times a year, and more often during treatment. Your doctor will give you a schedule.

faq.q: If the virus is not detected, can I stop my pills?
faq.a: No. It means the treatment is working. Only your doctor can stop it.

reminders.text: Hepatitis B PCR tomorrow. Better to skip fatty food in the morning. Take medicines as usual.
